questions.question: How can you help reduce road rage?

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.

questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, follow all traffic laws, signs, signals, and road markings. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your body?
questions.explanation: Alcohol works quickly but leaves your body slowly. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower blood alcohol levels. Waiting is the only way to lower your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another car, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.explanation: Signal before changing lanes to alert other drivers. Always check your mirrors and turn your head to look at your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: A distraction while driving is:

options.text: Anything that takes your mind off driving.
Something that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your mind off driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anywhere and anytime. Distracted driving can cause crashes, injuries, and death.

questions.question: What color are temporary signs in construction zones?
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: What lights should you use in rain or fog?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, or fog. High beam headlights reflect off rain and fog, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of the road mean?

options.text: You can pass from both directions.
You can pass from your direction only.
No one can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double yellow line in the center means no one can cross it to pass from either direction.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines separating traffic lanes mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from the left.
Passing is allowed from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean no passing from either direction.

questions.question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: Children do not react as fast as adults.
Children are smaller and harder to see.

questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, and parks. They may ride bikes onto the road without warning.

questions.question: What should you do at a red traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to clear the intersection.

questions.explanation: Stop at a red light. Stay stopped until the light turns green.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing after the "Don't Walk" signal flashes and is in the middle of the street when your light turns green. What should you do?

options.text: Go if you have the right-of-way.
Go if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.
questions.explanation: At a green light, you must wait for any pedestrians, bicyclists, or vehicles in the intersection. Wait until they cross before proceeding.

questions.question: When must you yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle?

options.text: When a police officer orders you to stop.

questions.explanation: Stop at a red light. Always obey police officers directing traffic, even if signs or signals say something different.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads, what should you know?

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so slow down.
You can see better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires grip loose gravel and dirt less than pavement. Slow down on these roads. It takes longer to stop and you can skid easily when turning.

questions.question: Which of these can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Cough syrup and cold medicine with codeine or antihistamines.

questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. These include tranquilizers and sedatives, over-the-counter cough syrups and cold medicines with alcohol or antihistamines, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: You must obey school crossing guards:

options.text: Unless you do not see any children present.

questions.explanation: Always obey crossing guards near schools. They direct traffic to keep children safe.

questions.question: You have a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: You must let pedestrians cross first.
You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the intersection. Drivers must let pedestrians cross when turning.

questions.question: You are merging onto an interstate highway. What should you do?

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Look for a gap large enough to safely enter traffic. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap.

questions.question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?

options.text: Play the radio loudly to distract yourself.
Wait a few minutes to calm down.
Drive on the interstate to release stress.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect safe driving. Take time to calm down before driving so you can focus on the road.

questions.question: What should you do if you see an aggressive driver?
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to let aggressive drivers pass. Do not try to compete with other drivers on the road.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?

options.text: Speed up to get through quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down in work zones and follow posted speed limits. Workers may be present, so be alert.

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.explanation: You must see clearly from all windows before driving. Clean all windows and mirrors of snow, ice, and frost.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs slow your nervous system. They reduce alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black markings alert you to road conditions ahead. This sign warns that another road crosses the highway.

questions.question: When passing a large truck, what should you do?

options.text: Move back into your lane and slow down immediately.
Give the truck plenty of space before moving back into your lane.
Move back into the lane whenever you want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the truck plenty of space before moving back into your lane.
questions.explanation: Wait until you can see the truck's front in your mirror before changing lanes. Don't slow down. Trucks need twice as much space to stop as cars.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the road mean?
questions.explanation: Solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed. If both sides are solid yellow, no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns of slippery conditions. Wet pavement is dangerous and takes longer to stop on. Slow down when you see this sign.

questions.question: What does a red curb mean?
questions.explanation: Do not park, stand, or stop at a red curb.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They alert drowsy drivers when their vehicle leaves the travel lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert drowsy drivers when their vehicle leaves the travel lane.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibrations to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign.
